title: The Definite Article
subtitle: Se, sēo, þæt — seventeen forms, the key to every noun.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of The Definite Article.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: The definite article in Old English declines for case, number, and gender. Three genders (masculine, feminine, neuter), two numbers (singular, plural), four cases. Not all combinations have distinct forms, but you must learn all seventeen. The article often disambiguates the case of a noun when the noun ending is ambiguous.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: se cyning (the king, nom), þone cyning (the king, acc), þæs cyninges (of the king, gen), þǣm cyninge (to/for the king, dat)

items.prompt: What is the main concept of this lesson?

items.answer: Review the paradigm and example above.
